title: Quantum effects, quantum gravity and beyond Einstein
scope: Where general relativity meets quantum physics and where it may be modified. Semiclassical effects (vacuum fluctuations, quantum fields on curved backgrounds, the Unruh effect, Hawking radiation and temperature, Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, the laws of black-hole mechanics, evaporation, the generalized second law and the information problem); gravity as a quantum field (Planck scales, force carriers, graviton exchange, spin-2 polarizations and trace subtraction, non-renormalizability and effective field theory); geometric unification and extra dimensions (Kaluza-Klein theory, compactification, braneworlds); candidate quantum theories (string theory and its world-sheet mechanics, supersymmetry, holography and AdS/CFT, canonical, Euclidean and loop quantum gravity, twistors); quantum and philosophical cosmology at the frontier (cosmological constant problem, quantum cosmology, anthropic arguments, Weyl curvature hypothesis); and classical alternatives to general relativity (Brans-Dicke, torsion theories). Classical black-hole theorems, classical field theory, the PPN testing machinery, inflation and elementary quantum mechanics belong to their own domains.

concepts.title: Quantum gravity
concepts.summary: The still-missing theory that consistently combines general relativity with quantum theory; it is needed wherever gravity is strong and quantum effects matter at once, such as the Big Bang, black-hole singularities and the end of black-hole evaporation.
concepts.notes: SCH ch08 uses it as a reason to keep testing GR (extra fields might violate the equivalence principle); DIV ch01 frames it as the conflict between the physics of the very large and the very small.

concepts.title: Planck units
concepts.summary: The unique length, time and energy that can be formed from G, c and hbar: l_P = sqrt(hbar G/c^3) ~ 1.6e-35 m, t_P = sqrt(hbar G/c^5) ~ 5.4e-44 s and E_P = m_P c^2 ~ 1.2e19 GeV. They mark the scale at which quantum effects and gravity are expected to be simultaneously important, far beyond any accelerator.
concepts.notes: In geometrized units hbar itself has dimensions of length squared (SCH Table 8.1), so l_P = sqrt(hbar). SCH ch13 uses the Planck time to say where classical Big Bang conclusions stop being trustworthy; GA ch49 compares E_P with LHC and cosmic-ray energies.

concepts.title: Planck mass
concepts.summary: The mass sqrt(hbar c/G) ~ 2.2e-8 kg (about 1.2e19 GeV); in hbar = c = 1 units its square is the coefficient that makes the Einstein-Hilbert action dimensionless, so it sets how weakly gravity couples. It also marks where a black hole is so small that a single Hawking quantum carries a sizable fraction of its mass and semiclassical physics fails.
concepts.notes: Pitfall: GA ch48 matches m_P^2 to the Einstein-Hilbert coefficient loosely; the literal match gives the reduced Planck mass 1/sqrt(8 pi G) conventions (m_P^2 = 1/16 pi G), while its footnote quotes G^{-1/2}. The dimension-counting technique (R ~ 1/L^2, d^4x ~ L^4, so a mass squared is needed; in 5D a mass cubed) is folded in here.

concepts.title: Planck-scale localization limit
concepts.summary: Confining a particle to a region of size L needs energy of order hbar c/L, whose gravitational radius grows as L shrinks; the two meet at the Planck length, so no experiment can resolve smaller distances without forming a black hole. This is a common heuristic for why spacetime geometry itself should be quantized.

concepts.title: Vacuum fluctuations
concepts.summary: In quantum field theory the vacuum is not static: it continually creates short-lived virtual particle pairs, allowed by the energy-time uncertainty relation to borrow an energy Delta E for a time of order hbar/Delta E before annihilating.
concepts.notes: This is the only quantum ingredient of the heuristic Hawking-radiation argument in SCH ch11 and GA ch28.

concepts.title: Particles as quantized field excitations
aliases: quantum field theory picture of particles
concepts.summary: In quantum field theory each particle species is a quantized excitation of a field: a classical field whose wave solutions carry energy is promoted to an operator that creates and annihilates quanta. Gravitational waves, as excitations of the metric perturbation, would correspondingly be made of gravitons.

names: quantum field theory picture of particles

merged_from: quantum field theory picture of particles

concepts.title: Quantum field theory in curved spacetime
concepts.summary: The semiclassical framework in which quantum fields propagate on a fixed classical curved metric that is not itself quantized; it underlies the Unruh effect and Hawking radiation and fails when the back-reaction of the quanta on the geometry becomes large, near the Planck scale.

names: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

merged_from: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
concepts.notes: SCH ch07 only points to the standard monographs; the books use the framework implicitly in GA ch28 and SCH ch11.

concepts.title: Path integral (sum over histories)
concepts.summary: Feynman's formulation of quantum mechanics: the amplitude to go from one configuration to another is a sum of exp(iS/hbar) over every possible history, with S the classical action; classical motion emerges where neighbouring phases add constructively.

concepts.title: Spacetime foam
concepts.summary: The expectation that the metric, like any quantum field, has zero-point fluctuations that grow to order unity at the Planck length, so that at that scale no single smooth geometry describes space.

concepts.title: Unruh effect
concepts.summary: A uniformly accelerated observer in the Minkowski vacuum detects a thermal bath at temperature k_B T = hbar a/(2 pi c), whereas an inertial observer sees no particles; particle content therefore depends on the observer. For a = g the temperature is only about 4e-20 K.
concepts.notes: GA ch28 reruns the pair-splitting story across the Rindler horizon; near a Schwarzschild horizon a static observer is a Rindler observer, which links the two effects.

concepts.title: Horizon pair-creation picture
concepts.summary: A heuristic for Hawking radiation: a virtual pair forms just outside the horizon, one member crosses to where negative Killing energy is allowed and need not recombine, and the other escapes as a real quantum. Requiring the infalling partner to reach the horizon within the fluctuation lifetime gives an escaping energy of order hbar/M.
concepts.notes: SCH ch11 estimates hbar/8M, which is 0.86 of the mean thermal photon energy from the exact result; GA ch28 gets hbar/4M. DIV ch20 describes the pairs with a backward-in-time reinterpretation.

concepts.title: Hawking radiation
concepts.summary: Black holes emit thermal, black-body radiation because of quantum field effects near the horizon, and the energy carried away comes out of the hole's mass. Hawking's 1974 calculation showed that the spectrum is exactly thermal at the Hawking temperature.

concepts.title: Hawking temperature
concepts.summary: The temperature of a black hole's thermal emission, k_B T = hbar kappa/(2 pi); for Schwarzschild it is hbar c^3/(8 pi G M k_B), about 6e-8 K for one solar mass. It is inversely proportional to mass, so smaller holes are hotter.

concepts.title: Wick rotation and Euclidean periodicity
concepts.summary: Continuing time to imaginary values turns the near-horizon Schwarzschild metric into a flat plane in polar coordinates, which is smooth at the origin only if Euclidean time is periodic with period 8 pi M; since a thermal state has imaginary-time period hbar/k_B T, this reproduces the Hawking temperature.

concepts.title: Black-hole thermodynamics
concepts.summary: The correspondence in which a black hole behaves as a thermodynamic body: mass plays the role of internal energy, surface gravity (times hbar/2 pi k_B) of temperature and horizon area (times k_B/4 hbar) of entropy, so that dM = T dS and the area theorem acts as a second law.
concepts.notes: SCH ch11 foreshadows the area-entropy analogy in its list of theorems and completes it once Hawking radiation supplies a genuine temperature.

concepts.title: First law of black-hole mechanics
concepts.summary: Neighbouring stationary black holes obey dM = (kappa/8 pi) dA + Omega_H dJ + Phi_H dQ in G = c = 1 units, relating changes in mass to changes in horizon area, angular momentum and charge. Read with T = hbar kappa/2 pi, it is dM = T dS plus work terms.
concepts.notes: For Schwarzschild it reduces to dM = dA/(32 pi M), which both SCH ch11 and GA ch28 rearrange to identify the entropy.

concepts.title: Bekenstein-Hawking entropy
concepts.summary: The entropy of a black hole, S = k_B c^3 A/(4 G hbar) = k_B A/(4 l_P^2), one quarter of the horizon area in Planck units. It follows from the first law once the Hawking temperature is known, and its enormous size measures how much information about the collapsed matter the horizon hides.
concepts.notes: DIV ch20 motivates it statistically: no-hair allows many progenitors for one (M, J, Q), quantum theory makes their number finite, and the entropy is its logarithm.

concepts.title: Laws of black-hole mechanics
concepts.summary: Four statements about stationary black holes that mirror thermodynamics: surface gravity is constant over the horizon (zeroth), dM = kappa dA/8 pi + Omega dJ + Phi dQ (first), horizon area never decreases classically (second), and kappa cannot be reduced to zero in finitely many steps (third).
concepts.notes: GA ch28 gives the dictionary M to U, kappa to T, A to S. The third law forbids reaching an extremal hole, the analogue of the unattainability of absolute zero.

concepts.title: Negative heat capacity of black holes
concepts.summary: Because a Schwarzschild hole's temperature scales as 1/M, adding energy cools it and removing energy heats it: C = dM/dT = -hbar/(8 pi k_B T^2) in G = c = 1 units. A black hole therefore cannot sit in stable equilibrium with an infinite heat bath, and its evaporation runs away.

names: negative heat capacity of black holes

merged_from: negative heat capacity of black holes

concepts.title: Black-hole evaporation
concepts.summary: An isolated black hole loses mass to Hawking radiation at a rate proportional to 1/M^2 (horizon area times T^4), so it heats up as it shrinks and its lifetime scales as M^3: about 1e10 yr for 1e12 kg but roughly 1e67 yr for a solar mass. Real astrophysical holes are colder than the cosmic microwave background and are still growing.

names: black holes in the cosmic microwave background
quantum gravity at the end of evaporation

merged_from: black holes in the cosmic microwave background
quantum gravity at the end of evaporation
concepts.notes: Only holes lighter than about 4.5e22 kg (GA prints 4.5e23 kg, a conversion slip) are currently hotter than the 2.73 K CMB. The final Planck-scale stage lies beyond quantum field theory on a fixed background and needs quantum gravity; SCH ch11 describes a final gamma-ray burst.

concepts.title: Penrose diagram of an evaporating black hole
concepts.summary: The conformal diagram of a star that collapses and whose black hole later evaporates completely: the event horizon and spacelike singularity exist only for a finite stretch, after which a regular centre continues to future timelike infinity. It is drawn on the provisional assumption that nothing is left behind.

names: Penrose diagram of an evaporating black hole

merged_from: Penrose diagram of an evaporating black hole

concepts.title: Generalized second law
concepts.summary: The total of black-hole entropy (k_B A/4 hbar) plus ordinary entropy outside black holes never decreases. It rescues the second law when Hawking evaporation shrinks the horizon area, since the emitted radiation carries at least the entropy lost.

concepts.title: Unitarity of quantum evolution
concepts.summary: Closed quantum systems evolve by unitary operators, so the state at one time fixes the state at any other and information is never destroyed; this is why complete black-hole evaporation into thermal radiation would be troubling.
concepts.notes: Elementary quantum mechanics; kept here because the books invoke it only for the information problem. Reconciliation may move it to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum.

concepts.title: Black-hole information problem
concepts.summary: If a black hole evaporates completely into exactly thermal radiation, the quantum information in the matter that formed it seems to be destroyed, contradicting unitary evolution. Whether subtle correlations in the radiation, remnants, or new physics carry the information out is unresolved.
concepts.notes: GA ch28 lists remnants and a final explosion as proposed escapes and records Hawking's own view that information is lost; SCH ch11 suggests correlations seeded by the collapsing matter.

concepts.title: Field description of gravity
aliases: fields tell charges how to move
concepts.summary: Describing gravity by a field defined at every event, which each body both sources and responds to locally, instead of by direct action at a distance between bodies; in general relativity that field is the metric itself.
concepts.notes: GA ch42 pairs Wheeler's gravity slogan with an electromagnetic version (fields tell charges how to move; charges tell fields how to arrange themselves). Reconciliation may prefer action-principles-and-field-theory as owner.

concepts.title: Gravity as a spin-2 field on flat spacetime
concepts.summary: The programme, associated with Feynman's gravitation lectures, of treating weak gravity as a massless symmetric tensor field h_mu_nu on fixed Minkowski space, coupled to energy-momentum and quantized like other gauge fields. It reproduces linearized general relativity and gravitons, but the flat background is a useful fiction that fails beyond first order.
concepts.notes: GA ch47 notes the programme was informative but did not yield a working quantum gravity; GA ch45 warns that real spacetime is curved and the picture breaks for non-Lorentz coordinate changes.

concepts.title: Feynman diagram
concepts.summary: A pictorial shorthand for one term in the perturbative expansion of a scattering amplitude: external lines for incoming and outgoing particles, vertices for couplings, and internal lines for propagators of virtual particles.

concepts.title: Scattering amplitude
concepts.summary: The complex amplitude whose squared modulus gives the probability for incoming states to scatter into outgoing ones; at lowest order for exchange between two sources it has the form source times propagator times source.

concepts.title: Force-carrying particle
concepts.summary: In quantum field theory an interaction between two sources arises from the virtual exchange of a mediating particle (Yukawa's idea); the mediator's mass sets the range of the force and its spin sets the tensor character and sign of the interaction.

concepts.title: Yukawa potential
aliases: range of a force and mediator mass
concepts.summary: The static potential from exchanging a particle of mass m, proportional to e^{-r/lambda}/r with range lambda = hbar/(mc); it is the point-source solution of the static Klein-Gordon equation, and only a massless mediator gives a long-range 1/r law.

names: range of a force and mediator mass

merged_from: range of a force and mediator mass

concepts.title: Spin of the mediator and sign of the force
aliases: spin of the mediator and sign of the force
concepts.summary: Exchange of an odd-spin boson (such as the spin-1 photon) makes like charges repel and unlike charges attract, while exchange of an even-spin boson (spin 0 or 2) gives a force of one sign between all sources; universal attraction is why the graviton must have even spin.

names: spin of the mediator and sign of the force

merged_from: spin of the mediator and sign of the force

concepts.title: Field rank and particle spin
concepts.summary: Massless quanta of spin 0, 1 and 2 are described by a scalar, a vector (one-form) and a symmetric rank-2 tensor, and they couple to sources of matching rank: a density, a current and the stress-energy tensor. Hence photons carry spin 1 and gravitons spin 2.

concepts.title: Helicity
concepts.summary: The component of a particle's spin along its direction of motion: a polarization state of helicity h picks up a phase e^{i h theta} under a rotation by theta about the momentum. A massless particle of spin S has only the two helicities +S and -S, so photons have h = +-1 and gravitons h = +-2.
concepts.notes: Ownership received from gravitational-waves. GA calls the circular states spin +-1; strictly the quantity is helicity and its sign depends on the rotation convention. A graviton polarization pattern repeats after 180 degrees, and plus turns into cross at 45 degrees.

concepts.title: Photon exchange amplitude
concepts.summary: The lowest-order amplitude for two currents to interact by exchanging a virtual photon, J_a . J_b/k^2 with propagator -i eta/(k^2 + i epsilon). Using current conservation k_mu J^mu = 0 splits it into an instantaneous charge-density term, which is Coulomb's law, and a retarded term containing only the two transverse polarizations.
concepts.notes: The rehearsal for the graviton calculation. The i epsilon shift fixes causal boundary conditions around the pole k^2 = 0 and is dropped in GA ch47. The apparent instantaneity of the Coulomb term is an artefact of a non-covariant split.

concepts.title: Graviton
concepts.summary: The hypothetical quantum of the gravitational field: a massless particle of spin 2 with two helicity states. Its masslessness follows from the exact 1/r Newtonian potential and its even spin from the universally attractive character of gravity; it appears automatically in string theory.
concepts.notes: SCH ch02 cautions that the graviton is not well defined without a quantum theory of gravity. GA Exercise 47.4 estimates graviton emission rates (radiated power over hbar omega) for the Earth-Sun system, showing classical waves contain astronomically many quanta. Observational mass bounds live in gravitational-wave-astronomy (graviton-mass-bound).

concepts.title: Graviton exchange amplitude
concepts.summary: The lowest-order amplitude for two energy-momentum distributions to interact by exchanging one virtual graviton, built from the linear coupling h_mu_nu T^mu_nu: after trace correction it is (-T_a . T_b + (1/2) T_a T_b)/k^2. Energy-momentum conservation k_mu T^mu_nu = 0 separates it into instantaneous and propagating parts.

names: gravitational coupling h_{mu nu} T^{mu nu}

merged_from: gravitational coupling h_{mu nu} T^{mu nu}
concepts.notes: energy-momentum conservation in momentum space was received from action-principles-and-field-theory.

concepts.title: Newtonian limit of graviton exchange
concepts.summary: The instantaneous T^00 T^00 part of the graviton exchange amplitude Fourier transforms to the Newtonian potential energy between mass densities; its sign is opposite to the corresponding Coulomb term, which is why like gravitational sources attract.

concepts.title: Trace subtraction in graviton exchange
concepts.summary: A symmetric rank-2 source contains a scalar trace, so the naive graviton amplitude also exchanges a spurious spin-0 mode and shows three transverse structures; adding (1/2) T_a T_b/k^2 cancels it and leaves only helicity +-2. The required factor 1/2 is exactly the trace reversal of the Einstein equation, obtained without geometry.
concepts.notes: Ownership received from einstein-field-equations. The same term halves the instantaneous coefficient (absorbed into G), which is what gives light twice the Newtonian coupling; GA does not remark on this.

concepts.title: Graviton polarizations
aliases: plus and cross polarizations of the graviton
concepts.summary: For a graviton moving along z only the transverse traceless combinations T^11 - T^22 and T^12 couple to the propagating part of the exchange amplitude, giving plus and cross polarization tensors that match the two linear polarizations of classical gravitational waves; their circular combinations have helicity +-2.

concepts.title: Graviton propagator
concepts.summary: The tensor D that contracts two stress-energy tensors into the graviton exchange amplitude, T_a D T_b; in harmonic (de Donder) gauge it is proportional to (eta eta + eta eta - eta eta)/k^2, where the last product implements the trace subtraction.
concepts.notes: Reading the amplitude as h_mu_nu T_a^mu_nu gives the field of a source, reproducing the trace-reversed linearized Einstein equation.

concepts.title: Ultraviolet divergences and renormalization
concepts.summary: In perturbative quantum field theory, point-like interactions make loop integrals diverge at short distances; renormalization absorbs these divergences into a finite number of redefined parameters, which works for the Standard Model but not for gravity.

concepts.title: Non-renormalizability of perturbative quantum gravity
aliases: Planck-scale breakdown of the G E^2 expansion
concepts.summary: Because Newton's constant has dimensions of inverse energy squared in natural units, graviton scattering grows order by order like (G E^2)^n and its divergences cannot be absorbed into finitely many parameters. Perturbative quantum gravity is predictive only for energies far below the Planck energy.

names: Planck-scale breakdown of the G E^2 expansion
validity range of perturbative quantum gravity

merged_from: Planck-scale breakdown of the G E^2 expansion
validity range of perturbative quantum gravity
concepts.notes: GA ch47 compares Fermi's contact theory of beta decay, whose dimensionful coupling also signalled new physics (W and Z exchange) near its breakdown scale.

concepts.title: Effective field theory
concepts.summary: A description valid below some energy scale that keeps the terms in the action with the fewest derivatives and represents unknown short-distance physics by higher-derivative terms suppressed by powers of a small length; renormalization-group reasoning explains how its parameters depend on scale.

concepts.title: Higher-curvature corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action
concepts.summary: Scalar terms quadratic in curvature (R^2, R_mu_nu R^mu_nu, R_abcd R^abcd) added to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian with dimensionless coefficients times a length squared; they matter only where curvature radii approach that length, so they are invisible in ordinary tests.

names: higher-curvature corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action

merged_from: higher-curvature corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action

concepts.title: Effective field theory of gravity
aliases: gravity as a low-energy effective theory
concepts.summary: The view that general relativity, though non-renormalizable, can be quantized and used reliably for processes far below a cutoff near the Planck energy, with quantum corrections organized as higher-derivative terms; above the cutoff a more fundamental theory must take over.

concepts.title: Unification of fundamental interactions
concepts.summary: The programme of describing distinct interactions, originally gravity and electromagnetism and today gravity plus the Standard Model, as manifestations of one underlying theory; its ultimate form is sometimes called a theory of everything.
concepts.notes: DIV ch01 asks whether the chain of ever smaller constituents must end in an ultimate theory.

concepts.title: Extra spatial dimension
concepts.summary: An additional spacelike coordinate appended to the four of spacetime, labelled x^5 or z, so that events in the enlarged spacetime carry five labels; the linearized metric perturbation and its gauge law carry over to five dimensions unchanged in form.
concepts.notes: The label 5 rather than 4 is historical. GA ch48 motivates it as the place where an internal phase fibre can live.

concepts.title: Gauge transformation as a shift of the fifth coordinate
aliases: electromagnetic gauge change as 5D coordinate transformation
concepts.summary: If the mixed metric components are h_mu5 = l A_mu, the five-dimensional coordinate change x^5 -> x^5 + l chi(x^mu) reproduces exactly the electromagnetic gauge transformation A -> A - d chi, so electromagnetic gauge freedom becomes part of five-dimensional general covariance. With the fifth dimension compact, this is an independent rotation of the internal circle at each event.

names: gauge transformation as a shift of the fifth coordinate
Kaluza-Klein gauge transformation as rotation of the internal circle

merged_from: gauge transformation as a shift of the fifth coordinate
Kaluza-Klein gauge transformation as rotation of the internal circle

concepts.title: Compactification
concepts.summary: Making an extra spatial dimension finite and periodic, for example identifying z with z + 2 pi a so that every point of four-dimensional spacetime carries a tiny circle; physics at scales much larger than a is unchanged, which explains why the dimension is unobserved.

concepts.title: Kaluza-Klein metric
concepts.summary: The five-dimensional line element ds^2 = g_mu_nu dx^mu dx^nu + (dz + l A_mu dx^mu)^2, which packages the four-dimensional metric and the electromagnetic potential into one geometry; the bracket is invariant under the combined shift z -> z + l chi and A -> A - d chi.

concepts.title: Kaluza-Klein reduction
concepts.summary: Integrating the five-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert action over the compact circle: for the Kaluza-Klein metric the 5D Ricci scalar equals the 4D Ricci scalar minus F_mu_nu F^mu_nu/4, so pure 5D gravity yields 4D gravity plus Maxwell's Lagrangian, and the 4D Planck mass is fixed by m_P^2 = 2 pi a m_K^3.

names: Kaluza-Klein reduction of the Ricci scalar
relation between Planck mass and five-dimensional scale

merged_from: Kaluza-Klein reduction of the Ricci scalar
relation between Planck mass and five-dimensional scale
concepts.notes: GA quotes the curvature reduction in Example 48.1 and derives it in Exercise 48.1 with orthonormal coframes and Cartan's structure equations (a cartan-method-for-curvature application). The 5D action carries a mass cubed m_K^3 for dimensional reasons.

concepts.title: Electric charge as momentum in the fifth dimension
aliases: Lorentz force from five-dimensional free motion
concepts.summary: A neutral particle moving freely in the Kaluza-Klein geometry obeys, in the four ordinary dimensions, the Lorentz force law, with its conserved momentum around the compact circle (times l) playing the role of electric charge. Charge becomes motion in the hidden direction.

names: Lorentz force from five-dimensional free motion
electric charge as momentum along the fifth dimension

merged_from: Lorentz force from five-dimensional free motion
electric charge as momentum along the fifth dimension

concepts.title: Charge quantization in Kaluza-Klein theory
concepts.summary: A single-valued quantum wavefunction around a circle of radius a allows only momenta p = n hbar/a; since charge is l times that momentum, every electric charge is an integer multiple of an elementary unit l/a.

concepts.title: Kaluza-Klein theory
concepts.summary: The theory in which four-dimensional spacetime is extended by a fifth spatial dimension compactified on a small circle, so that pure five-dimensional gravity reproduces four-dimensional gravity plus electromagnetism, with gauge transformations as circle shifts and charge as circle momentum. It is the prototype of geometric unification and of extra dimensions in string theory.

concepts.title: Kaluza-Klein tower
aliases: resolution energy of a compact dimension
concepts.summary: A quantum particle that can move around a compact dimension of radius a has its momentum there quantized in units of hbar/a, adding a ladder of heavy states above the ordinary ones; since probing the extra dimension needs momentum of order hbar/a, a microscopic a hides it from all low-energy experiments.

names: resolution energy of a compact dimension

merged_from: resolution energy of a compact dimension

concepts.title: Gravity in higher dimensions
concepts.summary: With d spatial dimensions Newtonian gravity spreads its flux over a (d-1)-sphere, so the force falls as 1/r^(d-1); if some dimensions are compact with volume V_c, distant observers see ordinary inverse-square gravity with G = G^(D)/V_c. The weakness of gravity could thus reflect large extra dimensions, and the true higher-dimensional Planck length could be much larger than l_P.

names: gravitational force law in d spatial dimensions
relation between higher-dimensional and observed gravitational constants

merged_from: gravitational force law in d spatial dimensions
relation between higher-dimensional and observed gravitational constants

concepts.title: Relativistic string
concepts.summary: A one-dimensional extended object with no internal parts, taken as fundamental in string theory; it carries a tension T0 (energy per unit length) that plays the role rest mass plays for a point particle, and its vibration modes appear as different particle species.

concepts.title: World sheet
aliases: induced metric on the world sheet
concepts.summary: The two-dimensional surface X^mu(tau, sigma) swept out by a moving string, the analogue of a particle's world line; the spacetime metric induces on it a 2x2 metric gamma_ab = eta_mu_nu dX^mu/dxi^a dX^nu/dxi^b.

names: induced metric on the world sheet

merged_from: induced metric on the world sheet

concepts.title: Nambu-Goto action
concepts.summary: The action of a relativistic string, minus its tension times the proper area of its world sheet, S = -T0 integral sqrt(-gamma) dtau dsigma; it is invariant under relabelling of the world sheet, and its Euler-Lagrange equations state that the world-sheet momentum currents are conserved.

concepts.title: World-sheet reparametrization gauge
concepts.summary: Because the Nambu-Goto action does not depend on how the world sheet is labelled, the parameters tau and sigma may be chosen to simplify the equations, like choosing an affine parameter for a world line. The static gauge tau = t makes each constant-tau curve the string at one coordinate time.

concepts.title: String wave equation
concepts.summary: In static gauge, with sigma chosen so the velocity is normal to the string, the Nambu-Goto equations reduce to the wave equation d^2X/dt^2 = d^2X/dsigma^2 plus constraints; only the transverse velocity is physical, and solutions are left- and right-moving waves that would become particles after quantization.

concepts.title: Open and closed strings
concepts.summary: An open string has two endpoints, which may be free or attached to branes, and sweeps out a ribbon-like world sheet; a closed string is a loop sweeping out a tube. The massless spin-2 graviton appears among closed-string states.

concepts.title: D-brane
concepts.summary: An extended object of p spatial dimensions on which the endpoints of open strings are fixed; the D stands for the Dirichlet boundary conditions that pin the endpoint coordinates transverse to the brane.

concepts.title: String theory
concepts.summary: A candidate unified quantum theory in which elementary particles are vibration modes of tiny strings in higher-dimensional spacetime; because it contains a massless spin-2 graviton and softens the short-distance divergences of point-particle graviton exchange, it is a quantum theory of gravity, but it lacks direct experimental confirmation.
concepts.notes: GA ch49 Example 49.4 contrasts a point Feynman vertex with a smooth string junction to show why strings improve ultraviolet behaviour. DIV ch01 describes it as the largest research effort in the area.

concepts.title: Supersymmetry
concepts.summary: A proposed symmetry that turns bosons into fermions and vice versa, giving every particle a superpartner of opposite statistics; since no equal-mass partners are seen it must be broken if it exists, and its lightest partners are dark-matter candidates.
concepts.notes: GA ch49 gives the naming rules: fermionic partners end in -ino, bosonic partners gain an s- prefix.

concepts.title: Superstring theory
concepts.summary: String theory with supersymmetry, whose Planck-length strings have both bosonic and fermionic states; its various versions are thought to be limits of a single M-theory that also contains higher-dimensional membranes, though none has yet produced falsifiable predictions.

concepts.title: Braneworld
concepts.summary: A scenario, arising from string theory, in which our universe is a four-dimensional brane in a higher-dimensional bulk: non-gravitational forces are confined to the brane while gravity extends into the bulk, modifying the inverse-square law at short distances (tested down to tens of micrometres). Matter on a nearby parallel brane would be felt only through gravity.
concepts.notes: SCH ch13 cautions that the dramatic scenarios come from deliberately simplified model theories.

concepts.title: Holographic principle
concepts.summary: The proposal, associated with 't Hooft and suggested by black-hole entropy scaling with area, that the physics of a gravitating region can be fully encoded by degrees of freedom on its lower-dimensional boundary, as a hologram stores a 3D image on a 2D plate.

concepts.title: AdS/CFT correspondence
concepts.summary: Maldacena's conjecture that certain quantum gravity (string) theories in (d+1)-dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetime are exactly equivalent to conformal field theories without gravity on its d-dimensional timelike boundary, with the radial bulk direction corresponding to energy scale in the boundary theory.

names: timelike conformal boundary of anti-de Sitter space

merged_from: timelike conformal boundary of anti-de Sitter space
concepts.notes: The timelike conformal boundary of AdS (DIV ch25 derives it on the Einstein static cylinder; light reaches it and returns in finite coordinate time) is where the boundary theory lives and makes AdS behave like a box. Folded here because anti-de-sitter-spacetime in cosmological-dynamics does not carry it.

concepts.title: Canonical quantization of gravity
concepts.summary: Quantizing general relativity by first putting it in Hamiltonian form, where constraints generate the gauge freedom, and then promoting the canonical variables (for example Ashtekar variables) to operators that must annihilate physical states.
concepts.notes: d'Inverno and Vickers mention their own variant built on a 2+2 splitting (see 2-plus-2-formalism).

concepts.title: Superspace (space of 3-geometries)
concepts.summary: Wheeler's configuration space for quantum geometrodynamics: the set of all spatial 3-geometries, to each of which a quantum state assigns an amplitude; a classical spacetime is a single path through it, while a quantum state spreads over many.
concepts.notes: Not to be confused with the superspace of supersymmetric field theories.

concepts.title: Einstein-Hamilton-Jacobi equation
concepts.summary: General relativity in Hamilton-Jacobi form: a functional differential equation for an action S on superspace, quadratic in dS/dgamma_ij through the DeWitt supermetric plus a 3-curvature term, which with the momentum constraint encodes the Einstein equations and is the semiclassical limit of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation.

concepts.title: Euclidean quantum gravity
concepts.summary: Hawking's approach that defines quantum-gravity amplitudes as path integrals over Riemannian (positive-definite) metrics obtained by rotating time to imaginary values; its simplest success is recovering black-hole temperature and entropy from smooth Euclidean geometries.

concepts.title: Angular momentum algebra
concepts.summary: The commutation relations [L_i, L_j] = i hbar epsilon_ijk L_k imply that L^2 takes the values hbar^2 j(j+1) with integer or half-integer j and that only L^2 and one component can be sharp at once; it is the model for how commutators generate quantization.
concepts.notes: Elementary quantum mechanics recalled in GA ch49 only to motivate area quantization; owned here because electromagnetism-thermal-quantum does not carry it.

concepts.title: Loop quantum gravity
concepts.summary: A non-perturbative approach that quantizes spatial geometry directly and finds discrete spectra for area and volume at the Planck scale, so the smooth manifold is replaced by a network of quantum cells; in cosmological applications the Big Bang can become a bounce.

concepts.title: Quantum of area
concepts.summary: If the area vectors of a tetrahedron's faces (which classically sum to zero, the closure condition) obey angular-momentum-like commutators with a Planck-scale constant, each face area takes only discrete values proportional to sqrt(j(j+1)) and the directions of face normals cannot all be sharp, so geometry is fuzzy at the Planck scale.
concepts.notes: GA Exercises 49.9-49.10 prove closure and the classical volume formula V^2 = (2/9) L1 x L2 . L3.

concepts.title: Quantum of volume
concepts.summary: In the quantized tetrahedron the volume operator commutes with the four face areas and the closure constraint, so states can be labelled by four spins and a volume eigenvalue, and volume changes only in discrete steps.

concepts.title: Spin network
concepts.summary: The graph that labels a quantum state of geometry in loop quantum gravity: nodes are chunks of volume, links are shared faces carrying area quanta, and closed paths through the graph are the loops that give the theory its name.

concepts.title: Quantum gravity bounce
concepts.summary: The proposal, found in loop quantum cosmology and other approaches, that quantum-gravity effects halt a collapse or a backward-extrapolated expansion before a singularity forms, producing a rebound; a Big Bang would then be a bounce from an earlier contracting phase.

concepts.title: Spinor
concepts.summary: An object transforming under the spin group, the double cover of the Lorentz group; two-component complex spinors live in a 2D space whose metric is antisymmetric, and vectors and tensors can be built from them, giving an efficient language for relativity and quantum physics.
concepts.notes: SCH ch03 uses spinor space only as an example that a metric need not be symmetric.

concepts.title: Twistor theory
concepts.summary: Penrose's programme that recasts spacetime geometry in a complex projective space of twistors, in which light rays rather than events are fundamental, as a possible route to quantum gravity.

concepts.title: Cosmological constant problem
concepts.summary: If the cosmological constant is the zero-point energy of quantum fields, naive estimates of the vacuum energy density exceed the observed dark-energy density by tens to over a hundred orders of magnitude, and why Lambda is so small remains unexplained.
concepts.notes: GA Exercise 15.5 estimates the discrepancy with strong-interaction scales; GA ch49 quotes about fifty orders (after Zel'dovich 1968); DIV ch26 quotes more than a hundred, the size depending on the assumed cutoff.

concepts.title: Quantum cosmology
concepts.summary: The application of quantum theory to the universe as a whole, needed for the earliest epochs near the Planck time and entangled with the interpretation problems of quantum mechanics, since there is no outside observer.

concepts.title: Weyl curvature hypothesis
concepts.summary: Penrose's conjecture that the initial cosmological singularity had very small or zero Weyl curvature, unlike black-hole singularities, so the universe began in an extremely smooth, low gravitational-entropy state that accounts for the thermodynamic arrow of time.

concepts.title: Conformal cyclic cosmology
concepts.summary: Penrose's proposal of an endless sequence of aeons in which the conformally rescaled remote future of one universe becomes the Big Bang of the next; it is offered as an alternative to inflation.

concepts.title: Anthropic principle
concepts.summary: The explanatory stance, named by Carter, that observed features of the universe are constrained by the requirement that observers like us can exist in it, so some apparent coincidences are selection effects.
concepts.notes: DIV ch26 offers it as an alternative to inflation for why the cosmological principle holds.

concepts.title: Weak anthropic principle
concepts.summary: Only some regions or epochs of the universe allow life, so we necessarily observe one of them; for example we find the universe billions of years old because galaxies, heavy elements, planets and evolution take that long.

concepts.title: Strong anthropic principle
concepts.summary: In d'Inverno and Vickers's version: among many universes (quantum branches, or disjoint regions with their own conditions or laws) only a few permit life, so the apparent fine-tuning of fundamental constants is a selection effect rather than evidence of design.
concepts.notes: DIV ch26 raises three objections to it. Stronger formulations in the literature (the universe must produce observers) differ from the book's.

concepts.title: Arrows of time
concepts.summary: The distinct directions singled out in time: the thermodynamic arrow of increasing entropy, the cosmological arrow of expansion and the psychological arrow of experience; why they agree is an open question sometimes tied to low-entropy initial conditions or anthropic reasoning.
concepts.notes: Ownership received from causal-structure-and-singularities.

concepts.title: Alternative theories of gravity
concepts.summary: Relativistic, generally covariant theories of gravity other than general relativity, usually with extra fields besides the metric; the physical criteria behind Einstein's equations do not single them out uniquely, but precision tests since the 1960s have excluded many rivals and none is simpler.

concepts.title: Brans-Dicke theory
concepts.summary: The 1961 scalar-tensor alternative to general relativity, motivated by Mach's principle, in which a dynamical scalar field sets the effective gravitational constant so that G can vary with cosmic epoch; its coupling omega gives PPN gamma = (1 + omega)/(2 + omega), recovering general relativity as omega -> infinity.

names: Machian variation of the gravitational constant

merged_from: Machian variation of the gravitational constant
concepts.notes: DIV ch09 argues that if inertial mass depends on the rest of the universe then G carries cosmic information and could vary; ownership of the PPN target received from orbits-light-and-tests. Solar-system bounds on gamma force omega to be very large.

concepts.title: Torsion-based theories of gravity
concepts.summary: Formulations such as Einstein-Cartan and teleparallel gravity in which the connection has torsion, so that torsion carries gravitational effects alongside or instead of curvature; Einstein-Cartan theory couples torsion to the spin density of matter.

out_of_scope_candidates.note: Used here as the temperature in the laws of black-hole mechanics.

out_of_scope_candidates.note: GA ch05 margin note on exotic matter for the warp drive; fold into alcubierre-warp-drive or energy conditions.
